I just quit the game on floor 4-5 (of 13) out of boredom. There is a lot to like about this game, the theme is great, the character based deck items are fun & exploring the synergies between the different protagonists is satisfying. That said, for me there are many more gripes and missed opportunities than aspects worthy of praise. -Map exploration is slow & becomes tedious after just a few runs there are some random story/combat encounters between room exploration but you will see the majority of them in just a few runs. Worst offender on this point is the very slow animations for getting on and riding the lift. -The mini-map should work to fast travel back to previously encountered rooms (backtracking across the whole floor after finding the elevator room behind the first door is just a huge waste of time). -The character/passive unlock system is probably the laziest I've ever seen in a roguelite game. You unlock characters via playing repeatedly, no other conditions as far as I've seen. There are so many compelling ways to handle item/character unlocks in this genre (pull off an intended synergy, do x amount of curse damage, complete a floor without taking damage etc.) but here we have 'do one run', 'do 3 runs', 'do 5 runs'. -Seemingly shallow item/synergy pool. In a lot of ways Spirit Lift feels like 'Babies first Deckbuilder' I enjoyed my first few runs as I played through and discovered how the different party characters interacted but ultimately there is very little mechanical depth to the combat. -Boss mechanics are all over the place. First run was a walk in the park, got to the mushroom vampire boss and steamrolled it. All the other bosses I've encountered have mechanics that will REQUIRE luck was on your side throughout the run to counter. Roguelite deckbuilders feel the most satisfying when the balance allows the player to use tactics & knowledge to overcome dire situations, poorly balanced games require lucky RNG. -The meta-progression is stingy and I'm not even sure how it's earned (assume just PLAY MORE RUNS). -The price point seems very off. This isn't an early access game, so, there is no expectation of additional content. As it sits I've had about 4 hours of fun for a game that cost $18 on sale. Compare that to Binding of Isaac or Noita or Vampire Survivors, I've gotten thousands of hours of excitement from those games at a similar (or dramatically lower) cost. If this game had been 7 or 8 bucks I don't think I would've felt as negatively about these flaws but asking 20 dollars for a game the is much less polished than it's similarly priced genre contemporaries is pretty egregious. Ambience/Vibes - 7/10 Gameplay - 5/10 Value - 3/10

All I can say is: Mixed. On one side it is simply a good and fairly polished game. On the other it isn't a roguelite where you get rewarded and stronger, but punished on every second turn. And there is nothing wrong with that, in principle, I just don't think it is that much fun getting punished by RNG, often with no way to anticipate or defend against it. Other than that, it suffers a little bit of the typical roguelike problem of item utility: Gear/Artifacts can be incredibly useful, but also essentially useless, making your run depending on your pulls in the end - meh. Still, didn't feel right to give this game a "Don't recommend", as it still has the typical draw of "one more run".

>Person who's only experience with Single Player Deckbuilders being played Midnight Suns "I'm getting a lot of Midnight Suns vibes from this" This game hasn't had a lot of attention to it yet so contributing what I can. Stuff I Love The deckbuilding and gameplay genuinely just feels like what I enjoyed about Midnight Suns but condensed so everyone shares the same health pool... I'm aware this is like a genre of it's own but I haven't really played Slay the Spire, the only other card games I've played are Marvel Snap and Magic the Gathering With hundreds of cards to collect and permutations to try out there's a lot to do before things can feel played out. Granted the uniqueness / how novel each party combination is isn't really that huge. I think this was a nice taster into the genre, I can see myself coming back to this style of gameplay. I also like how brief each runs are, like just an hour, even if a run feels like it's going pear-shaped the relative progression does sorta encourage you to keep going because even a failed run will get some unlocks from the Library. Finally I just love the aesthetic and the theming. It reminds me somewhat of the Arkham Horror LCGs, in fact that connection is what made me pull the trigger for this over like the dozens of other Deckbuilding Roguelites ~ Stuff I Personally Do Not Like; The Grind, I'm 30 hours in almost and I'm like ~50% through the Library and I'm still nowhere near close unlocking any Alternate Endings... I feel like they could have halved that and this would have been a fine experience.... and also honestly some of the Challenges can be a bit mad too and feel designed to be cheesed. Lack of Variety in Dungeon Modifiers, the Lift Levels are kinda boring, I thought they'd be more like DD2 Torches where each level has some distinct feels to them and... no not really. It's just the previous Lift Level + another Modifier. Like there's no real reason to revisit earlier Lift Levels. But honestly these are just me.

Really fun rouge like horror card battler with some pretty interesting story added. My only complaint so far is that the game seems TOO easy. I am now 4 runs in beaten 4 boses and haven't lost a single run yet. I think my first run was the closest....but after you figure out balancing dodge + purify the game seems to be just a time sink. Excited to unlock more and hoping there is a lot more secrets to uncover :) Gameplay - 8 Sound - 10 (slaps) Aesthetics - 9 Story - 8

A decent 8/10 turn based adventure spooky game. But you have all the usual: - RNG kindof sucks. - not that many enemy variety. - sometimes the UI gets in the way. - too grindy.. - the best characters are unlocked last. - unity engine.. - too expensive for what it offers even if the style is nice.

It's okay. The influence from slay the spire is clear but it does its own thing too, mixing the haunted house style into a lightweight deckbuilder. Cards having durability is an interesting concept. Music is good. The characters add some interesting variety. My main issue is that the cards you find in your journey mostly suck. You will probably make your deck worse by taking them. I ended the run with just my starter deck plus a few upgrades and relics. The events seem to offer a lot of curses for very minor benefits, which means most of the time you just click "no", which is a shame. The enemies are quite repetitive, they mostly seem to be the same 3-4 colourswapped enemies with slightly bigger numbers. Would be great to have more variety.

When I die, I hope someone immortalizes my life in a game like this The Spirit Lift is truly a hidden gem. At the time of writing there's only 111 reviews on Steam, mostly positive. More people need to know about this game. It's in my top 5 deckbuilding games of all time and personally I enjoyed it more than the likes of Slay the Spire, Balatro, etc and I'll outline why below On the surface the game appears almost like some AI jank with the way the graphics are presented, very minimal art for chaacters, no audio voicelines, opting for text instead Story wise, you are thrust into a hotel with 3 teenagers seemingly bored at a party and finding a secret elevator lift which you unsurprisingly take to the upper floors Gameplay wise a run consists of a navigating up to 13 floors culminating in a final boss fight on the 13th floor Music throughout the game is pretty fire and sets the tone and keeps you engaged in the atmosphere. It truly feels like you're in some creepy hotel trying to look for an escape route When I first played the game I didn't know why it was called that but as I went through different floors and hotel rooms, it was difficult to not see my spirit being lifted with every interesting piece of lore discovery. It was as if I was reading a really interesting novel. The more I learned, the more I wanted to learn It took me 55 hours to unlock all the starting cards and starting gears for all of the 8 characters. For some, this may be a grind but it never felt like that to me. I was so wrapped up in the gameplay and thinking of which combination of characters could optimally achieve the unlockables If you are looking for a game to lift your spirits, this is it Thank you to the devs. If you're reading this, I absolutely enjoyed every minute of this game. If you are still updating the game, I'd love to see more creature types (and bosses) being added to the game. Maybe some more starting characters as well like how about a blonde hair girl character and a black hair asian guy character to round out the roster? I love all of them dearly and play them all in different teams (my favorite combo is either Happy Go Lucky or The Sixth Sense or The Study Group). They are all quite viable but I would suggest if Garnet could use a starting card (or gear) that conditionally adds trauma cards to your own deck during a battle for easier deckbuilding synergy. Also when activating tool cards, it sometimes covers up the left most monsters intention (e.g. if they are planning to attack you it may hide the attack strength). I remember the tall mushroom dude that spawns shroomcakes being such a case for example

To be honest, there is nothing really wrong with this game. On all points it does fairly alright. The problem is that if it is a roguelike, the gameplay cycle needs to be fresh and rewarding each cycle. And this just isnt. It dripfeeds you rewards at a pace that should be 2-3x faster at the very least and it doesn't allow you to speed anything up. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ elevator transition has no right to not be sped up if you have to go through it after each floor. Yeah, fun mediocre until the novelty wears off.

I don't recommend this based on lack of controller support, and the amount of time wasted with animations (with no option to streamline them or skip them). It's cozy enough, but its's just bait for completionists, and torture bait at that. The game is super easy to win, and doesn't drastically change with new characters.

Honestly wished I knew about this game sooner. I love deck builders in general and this was no exception. Love the spooky but fun Halloween vibes. Is it the greatest deck builder? No, I'd say the RNG is rough at times and the progression can be stagnant but honestly for what it is it was an incredibly fun time.
Fun deckbuilder, moving around feels a bit slow in places but the combat it solid.

Solid game, very interesting concept, loving the music, still playing through it and unlocking everything. Finding some crazy cards, powerful combos, stuff you would expect from a deck builder. Noticing a lot of people giving it a negative review and have only about an hour of gameplay, which leads me to believe they just didn't read, explore, or appreciate anything. Love the references to various things, such as the jack in the box with a skateboard saying "Hello fellow teens" Love that meme. I certainly hope they keep adding to this game, more mysteries and story, more enemies, more cards, more events and environments, more music! Keep up the good work!

This game is definitely the most hidden gem I've played in a long time! I'm honestly surprised that more people don't know about it and that it's more popular. It's a really fun rogue-lite deckbuilder game and has pretty much everything you would want or expect and it has a lot of replay value and things to unlock! My only complaints with the game is that I wish there were at least one more party member of each type in order to have parties that are fully focused on doing a specific thing and having more characters wouldn't be a bad thing in general (there are like 8 characters in this game and 3 to a party) and the elevator loading screens to reach the next area take too long. I would definitely recommend this game if it looks interesting or you like rogue-lite deckbuilder games because it will definitely bring you some fun and there is a lot to do in the game surprisingly! I have 18 hours in the game and I'm far from doing everything in the game (although beating the game itself is relatively short which is around an hour).

This game just feels uninspired. I won my first run mainly relying on mostly starter cards, and was bored halfway through it. There was maybe 5 enemy types, and on the final floors you fight the same enemies you fought on the first floor, just with higher stats. They all have animations as uninteresting as their mechanics. I was expecting there to be a twist because the final boss just seemed like a regular enemy, but no, the run just ended. I unlocked another character and meta progression, but don't feel like doing another run at all because of the uninteresting gameplay.

Pros: Deep deck building that has room for plenty of strats to shine, from card spam to Turtling I love the characters and their little interactions with each other. Forming teams with unique names is nice touch. the aesthetic is very appealing with the haunted hotel setting in full swing here. Lots of unlockables to keep runs fresh with new strats to pursue Cons: The overall presentation of a run gets old kinda fast The grind is gonna take you a while to get unlocks Floors are over too quickly when they could be filled with more rooms of chance and random battles. This would give players a risk/reward system of either choosing to take the lift now and avoid further battles or try to complete more rooms and fights for loot. At the moment, you might as well clear every floor before taking the lift. No voice acting + No impactful effects to cards leave repeated runs feeling like you are just playing the same game multiple times without much variety despite using a completely new way to play. (this may be a personal thing) I hated the elevator rides; each floor requires an unskippable elevator ride to the next where you get a short blurb from your party. This is a slow and calming moment that you will have to sit through multiple times across multiple runs full of strategizing, high risk fights, monsters, and difficult choices that all comes to a sudden halt when you get in. It gives me so much whiplash. Lastly, the monsters in general need more variety
This game is really good. I've got almost 100 hours in it and I'm not exactly sure why, but it's obviously replayable. Get it.

This is yet another clever, fun take on the roguelite card battler. I really enjoy the art style and the punny names, as well as the sprinkling of lore that you get as you make your way through. The concept of having a 'team' to represent your deck, with the ability (and encouragement from the game) to mix-and-match each team member, is something I genuinely have not seen before, and adds a ton of replayability to a core loop that can be slightly lacking in that area. This is not an earth-shattering video game by any means. But there are enough unique quirks here to make it stand out in a crowded field, the game loop is satisfying, and I like the characters a lot. (Also I just f'ing LOVE me a haunted hotel, haha.) I've played 22 hours of this so far, and I think all of that was within the span of, like, three days. I haven't touched it since, but I'm extremely confident in predicting that in a couple of months, I'll boot this up again for another dip, and then spend another three days obsessively playing more of it; rinse and repeat. If you're of a similar mind, I think you'll absolutely vibe with this game.

I adore the presentation of this game. The atmosphere is on point, the graphics are nice, the little bits of lore are intriguing, and the the soundtrack is quite fitting. It's just a shame that as a deckbuilder, there is so much that falls flat. Enemies are constantly reused and recolored. There's a large pool of things to unlocked, but so much is locked from the beginning that you see the same things repeatedly. Their attack patterns are uninspired: most enemies can be divided into a pattern of "attack, then apply a negligible debuff". Balancing is extremely poor: some rare gear was worthless, while a common gear went infinite with just the cards in the starting deck. Runs are a slog: way too much time is just snooping around in hallways and elevator animations. The great presentation can't save a bad game. This is easily my biggest gaming disappointment of 2026 so far.

It's fairly decent and I thought I liked it for one run, then I went off it quite a bit on a second run, then I'm just furious with it on a third run. How can this possibly have been playtested without anyone saying "how about we let people skip the elevator animation, it takes forever and is boring". How is there a config option for speed of walking and turning animations but *not* at least an option to *accelerate* the much slower elevator animation? The *default* walk speed is already three times faster than the speed at which the characters walk the first square out of the elevator, the max speed is even higher, which makes that sluggish elevator exit all the more excruciating by comparison. The pace of unlocks is also glacial, it takes three long runs to unlock enough points to refund the points you spent on a crappy 10% increase in base health and something else irrelevant, for an extra equipment slot, which is *also* fairly paltry, and it looks like another two entire runs after that to unlock a different unlock tree. It's three runs to unlock a new character. If this was the only game available then the glacial pace would maybe be a selling point, but in a world with thousands of games at our fingertips, why would anyone want to play a game that's almost exactly the same every time, three times, to unlock making it *slightly* different for the next run. Could have been a decent game (even ignoring these flaws it's not *great*, but I would have rated it a soft recommend) but these awful arbitrary decisions to not just *reduce some delays* makes it a pretty hard unrecommend.

Spirit Lift doesn't quite reach the Penthouse. The Good: Graphics and Sound track do a good job of relaying the atmosphere. I love the throwback and horror vibes it has going and the bit of lore to the characters is quite interesting. The Bad: Gameplay is nice, but there isn't enough variety to make justify the grind to gain all the rewards/achievements. 54 Party compositions to try out with each of the three characters having a number of options to swap between runs is nice, but there are 4 bosses and each boss has it's own group of monster with about 2 other sprite groups. There are a about 3 or so "palette swap" monster per sprite group that act functionally different, it still gets old pretty quick when the expectation is to play at least 64 runs. The grind to gain 'power' to make your runs easier is also a bit slow. Tackling harder difficulties make it easier to get more, but the options feel a bit lackluster for the effort it takes to increase them.

Decent game, but in the spirit of Lovecraft gets increasingly challenging before becoming insane, so you'll progress further once you've worked out how to create a decent build and had a bit of luck on the pulls. Very hard but mostly fair, so far it's been a good game for a few idle run throughs on the sofa but I can see from the various secrets I've started to uncover that there's more depth to this ready to be revealed. Perfect Steam Deck compatibility for me, although I use trackpad mouse by default so ymmv.

A really polished roguelite deckbuilder with a unique premise and some fresh twists. It doesn't get bogged down in minutiae to maintain an engaging level of complexity, allowing battles to be both quick and strategic. And the music is excellent, getting you right in the mood for some ghost-bustin'. A minor complaint is that there isn't a huge level of enemy variety, with the game relying on palette swaps to pad out its roster of foes. Other than that, it's solid, and a great thematic contrast to other games in the genre.
its ok for what it is , but it just wastes to much time for transitions and such , it feels like it pads everything , plus its legability and such feels off

I can understand why not all fans of deckbuilders would like this game, but for me, it scratches just the right itches. It's about building synergies, and then making a small, highly-upgraded deck. If you like adding a lot of cards, this isn't your game. It also has rougelite meta-progression which makes the game MUCH easier, mostly in the form of adding passive healing and gold to each run. You don't unlock higher difficulty runs until you've defeated all four bosses, and since which boss you get is random, that can take a while. Even so, you'll be getting new characters to add to your team and try out the whole time, so it didn't get boring. I like the asthetic and the music, too. Overall, I've been liking this a lot.
i love this game, what a beautiful passion project, genuinely fun to play and such personality in the design with a hint of nostalgia

Genuinely one of my favourite titles from this genre, roping me back in day after day. The sheer variety of starting characters/gear/cards you can mix & match, and all the builds they can enable, really gives you a reason to come back and play run after run after run. There were also a not-insignificant number of times I thought I was reaching the end of things you can discover, only for the game to open up another layer of complexity. Additionally, it feels like there's more variety with statuses and cards than in other comparable games, and I can't put my finger on why, but the very act of deckbuilding has a distinctly different feel from its colleagues like Slay The Spire. Also, Dorian is hot.
oogh i love a roguelike deckbuilder. and i love horror. and i love lore. and i love maps. she's got it all

Of course it's not perfect, but for a game that was released at the beginning of this year, it's pretty damn good. roguelite with lore, check (honestly i'd love more of our player character's story, and potentially an ending for THEM, but i havent done everything there is to do yet so maybe that's coming) soundtrack with a variations on a theme style, love it. different boss options, hell yeah (i'd love a fifth). character interactions, awesome. (would love even more unique ones, like events that you can only access with a certain team. that would mean like another 56 events never mind.) i just want to know what happens after they win the fight at the penthouse. final thoughts, gameplay is awesome, i just want more story (and maybe an option to sell some relics to dorian). also tobias is the best.
7/10 Pretty good.
